semantics: Three separately identified witness candidates, one annual-order constituent stage and no revision transition. H14 is not a complete altar Missal or Mass Ordinary. F.1/101 and treasury 98/89 remain unpositioned and have no established local-use stage. Dates 1101–1300 bound palaeographic attestation, not years of use.

uses.stage_scope: Annual local ceremonial order in H14 ff. 47–74; printed excerpts and modern manuscript identity, not a complete altar Mass book.

stage_evidence.claim: Identifies the manuscript constituent, Monza origin and XII–XIII palaeographic dating.

Frisi prints the local-church attribution from still-legible vestiges of erased wording (p. 190, note 18); his excerpts give Christmas Mass and Communion and Easter baptismal, Mass and processional directions. Modern H14 identification is independently supported by the census and edition review.

stage_evidence.locus: Review of edition A chapters 4, 6, 9 and critical text: pp. 53–77, 251–276, 375–382, 431–541
stage_evidence.claim: Distinguishes calendar-obituary from order; attributes Roman rite according to Monza custom to the edition, with specific Ambrosian initiation parallels.

uses.date_role: H14 attestation, 1101–1300; no first-use or effectiveness date
uses.reception: The local order prescribes ceremonial practice for Monza. Frisi's local title attribution rests on still-legible erased wording; the census and edition review separately support H14 identity and classification. No first celebration, uniform observance or continuity through 1578 is established.
uses.limitations: No complete H14 text, original manuscript collation, exact copying year, promulgation act or revision is established. Liber ordinarius is an order book; its title does not identify a Mass Ordinary. Frisi associated copying with a 1256 bequest; that older report is not used to narrow the modern broad century range.

sources.inspection: Whole University of Illinois digitization acquired, 394 PDF pages. Printed pp. 190–191, 195 (PDF pp. 220–221, 225) visually inspected; other Monza catalogue passages read in extracted text. Entry CLXXXVII describes and partially edits the local order, historically Milan Cathedral B.43; printed pp. 79–82 describe F.1/101 under former E.III / CXXVI. This is an eighteenth-century witness to the manuscript and a partial edition, not original manuscript-image collation. Frisi III, p. 190, note 18, reports that the words identifying Ecclesia Modoetiensis were erased but still legible in vestiges; modern H14 identity and local-order classification are independently supported by the 2018 census and the critical-edition review.

Whole PIMS/University of Toronto digitization acquired, 510 PDF pages. Printed pp. 108–109 (PDF pp. 126–127) visually inspected for F.1/101 components; pp. 105–110 read with surrounding entries. Ebner explicitly had insufficient access time to settle leaf-order questions, p. 109. His older dating of the treasury sacramentary is superseded by later palaeography and is not adopted.

Whole Latinitas series nova VI (2018), vol. 1 acquired, 160 PDF pages. Baroffio, Sodi and Suski, I libri ordinari di origine italiana: guida ai manoscritti pretridentini, p. 73 (PDF p. 73), Monza entry visually inspected: H-14 ff. 47–74, Ordinarium, XII–XIII centuries, Monza; cites Dell’Oro–Mambretti (2001). Nearby B-14/121 is explicitly an Ambrosian Manuale fragment, not H14.

Complete university HTML review by Pietro Messa, Antonianum 78/1 (2003), pp. 187–190 acquired and read. It separates H14 calendar-obituary ff. 1–46 from local order ff. 47–74; identifies edition A pp. 53–77 parallel Mass/Office books, pp. 251–276 initiation, pp. 375–382 Roman rite according to Monza custom, and critical text pp. 431–541. Review evidence is not direct inspection of the 2001 edition.

Whole Hartmut Hoffmann, Zum 2. Band von Bernhard Bischoffs Katalog, Deutsches Archiv 61/1 (2005), pp. 53–72, with issue front matter acquired, 24 PDF pages. Printed p. 71 (PDF p. 23) expressly corrects the treasury Sacramentario di Berengario shelfmark from 89 to 98, at Bischoff record 2898. This conflicts with Westwell (2024)'s 89; do not erase the alias/conflict.

Current indexed IRHT record inspected through web search on 2026-10-20: Monza 98, Sacramentarium, 125 leaves, 265 × 140 mm, 846–855, origin Monza; bibliography Belloni–Ferrari, pp. 194–196, Bischoff II, no. 2898, Gamber II, no. 728. Whole raw IRHT delivery timed out for other exact pages in this lane; no newly acquired raw HTML or manuscript images are claimed. Date/origin conflict with Westwell is retained.

Whole AMS/SMT Indianapolis 2010 program and abstracts acquired. Daniel DiCenso, How One Source Could Change our Understanding of Chant Transmission: Monza Biblioteca Capitolare f. 1/101, printed pp. 208–209 (PDF pp. 177–178), read. Re-dates the chant unit to ninth-century Bergamo and reports 14 folios, disputing late/fragment labels. This abstract cannot date the entire composite codex or reconcile Ebner's ff. 1–11 count.

Whole cathedral bulletin November 2025 acquired, 36 PDF pages. Claudio Antonio Fontana, Servare et fovere, printed pp. 21–24, read. Discusses Roman books, Ambrosian holdings, missing patriarchine ritual exemplars, the local ordinary as a coordinating book, and the 1578 dispute. Reports 18 June and 16 October 1578 letters; original archival texts and their full instruments remain uninspected. No normative transition is created from this retrospective.

Current indexed Bibale record inspected through web search on 2026-10-20: H14 calendar-obituary and cathedral ordinary, 1101–1300; Monza before 1578, Milan 1578–ca 1800, Phillipps 7091, returned 1983. Direct raw HTML request timed out; no new full raw artifact is claimed. Broad catalogue chronology corroborates XII–XIII; custody is not continuous liturgical use.

Whole Arthur Westwell, The Carolingian Sacramentaries of Saint-Amand (2024), 514 PDF pages acquired. Introduction pp. 6–7, Appendix 2 pp. 419–425 (PDF pp. 445–451), and related discussion read; Appendix 2 p. 419 visually inspected. Distinguishes treasury Berengar (called Ms.89) from F.1/101. Catalogues Mass components and later additions by folio. The date, northeastern-French manufacture and possible Cysoing/Eberhard relationship remain the author's argument, not an established Monza local-use or donor-book edge.

versions.title: Monza H14 ff. 47–74, Liber ordinarius Modoetiensis
versions.locus: H14 ff. 47–74; Frisi (1794), vol. III, entry CLXXXVII, pp. 190–201, especially 190–191, 195; Baroffio–Sodi–Suski (2018) p. 73; Messa review of Dell’Oro (2001), volume A pp. 375–382 and 431–541.
versions.limitations: Local annual order-book witness, not an altar Missal or a complete Mass Ordinary. Calendar-obituary ff. 1–46 is a separate constituent. Roman rite according to Monza custom is the critical edition's conclusion reported in its review; initiation relationships with Milan do not make the whole book Ambrosian. Frisi's old Milan B.43 description is kept as historical custody, not a new book. Frisi III, p. 190, note 18, reports that the words identifying Ecclesia Modoetiensis were erased but still legible in vestiges; modern H14 identity and local-order classification are independently supported by the 2018 census and the critical-edition review.

versions.title: Monza F.1/101 composite Mass antiphoner, sacramentary and lectionary
versions.date: Constituent datings disputed: ninth-century chant unit argued; older catalogues IX–X or XI for codex
versions.locus: Ebner (1896) pp. 108–110, especially chant ff. 1–11 and sacramentary from f. 12; Frisi (1794), vol. III, CXXVI pp. 79–82, formerly E.III; DiCenso (2010) pp. 208–209 dates only the chant witness and gives 14 folios.
versions.limitations: Distinct from treasury Berengar 98/89. Composite Mass materials: no inference of one homogeneous date. Ebner describes Ambrosian traces in Canon and two Ambrose formularies alongside Roman prayer material, plus later corrections and incomplete lectionary. Monza custody and possible Bergamo origin do not establish Monza local reception. Dold–Gamber (1957) and Chavasse (1985) remain exact next editions, not read here.

versions.title: Monza treasury Sacramentary of Berengar, 98 (89 in some scholarship)
versions.date: Ninth century; IRHT 846–855 conflicts with Westwell's 860s before 867
versions.locus: Westwell (2024) introduction pp. 6–7 and Appendix 2 pp. 419–425: 125 leaves; Preface/Canon ff. 1v–5v, Gregorian body ff. 5v–115v; Hoffmann (2005) p. 71 corrects 89 to 98 (Bischoff 2898); IRHT 614133 gives 98.
versions.limitations: Named royal intercession at f. 48r and chapel inventories ff. 116v, 124v support a royal association, not a cathedral-wide Monza Eucharistic recension. Westwell's northeastern-French manufacture and Cysoing/Eberhard transfer are qualified arguments; IRHT origin Monza is not silently adopted as manufacture. No historical-parentage or local adoption edge is asserted.

checks.claim: H14 constituent, local order and broad date
checks.evidence: Latinitas VI.1 (2018), p. 73 original page image; Frisi III pp. 190–191,195 original printed-page images; independently fetched complete Messa review
checks.result: Supported. The 28-leaf order agrees with H14 ff. 47–74. Frisi supplies Christmas and Easter Mass/Communion directions, while modern census identifies the exact constituent. The modern edition’s Roman-local-custom conclusion remains explicitly mediated through Messa.
checks.limit: The original H14 and complete 2001 edition were not independently acquired. No wording collation or new textual transition is certified.

checks.claim: F.1/101 composition and distinction from treasury Berengar
checks.evidence: Ebner (1896), pp. 108–109 original page images and adjacent text; Westwell (2024) separate manuscript entries and Appendix 2; DiCenso AMS 2010 abstract pp. 208–209
checks.result: Supported. Ebner separates chant, sacramentary, Canon and concluding readings, acknowledges his inspection-time limit and identifies Ambrosian elements. The DiCenso abstract dates the chant material and reports fourteen folios; it must not date or reconstruct the whole composite.
checks.limit: Eleven versus fourteen folios and constituent dating remain unresolved. No local altar use is established.

checks.result: Supported as disagreements. Hoffmann corrects 89 to 98; Westwell retains 89 and proposes 860s before 867, with northeastern-French manufacture. IRHT gives 98, 846–855 and origin Monza. The proposed unpositioned candidate avoids silently harmonizing these claims.
checks.limit: Direct IRHT HTML timed out; only the current indexed record was independently reproduced. Catalogue origin does not prove manufacture or cathedral use.
